title: What Goes in Git Sorting Activity
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: A drag-and-drop sorting activity with ten robot project files. Students decide which files to commit to Git and which to put in .gitignore, while a live repository preview warns when a password file would become public and a generated .gitignore builds from the ignore bin.

educational.topic: Version control: choosing files to commit and files to ignore
learningObjectives: Classify robot project files as belonging in a Git repository or in .gitignore.
Explain why files that hold passwords must never be committed.
Explain why automatically generated files such as __pycache__ and .pyc files are ignored.
Recognize that library files the robot needs, such as vl53l0x.py, should be committed.
prerequisites: The git add and git commit workflow
The config.py pattern and module files
standards: CSTA 3A-NI-06: Recommend security measures to address various scenarios based on factors such as efficiency, feasibility, and ethical impacts

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Classification activity with delayed feedback and on-demand explanations
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Students drag file cards into two bins, watch the repository preview and generated .gitignore update live, then check answers and click cards to read the reasons.
keyQuestions: Which files would a teammate need to run your robot?
Which files hold secrets that must stay private?
Which files does your computer make automatically?
What should you do if you already committed a password?
commonMisconceptions: Library files like vl53l0x.py should be ignored because you did not write them.
config.py holds secrets and must be ignored (it only holds pin numbers).
Deleting a password file in a later commit removes it from the repository history.
Every file in the project folder belongs in the repository.
assessmentOpportunities: Challenge: explain what to do after committing secrets.py by mistake.
Exit ticket: name one file that must never be committed and one that must always be committed.
